questions.claims_summary: Counts for the selected organization’s documents in the window. A finding is a claim that states a result.

rows.basis: It states no method, population or setting

first_claims.summary: 1 claim to be first in the window: 0 contradicted, 0 not contradicted, 1 not checkable.

measures.cite: Share: Dirichlet-multinomial posterior. Missing articles: multi-list capture-recapture (Fienberg 1972).
measures.definition: Its share of the independent news articles found about the map’s reports. Copies of one wire story count once.
measures.how: Articles linked to a report by the propagation engine at its two strictest tiers (a link to the report, or the firm and the title named; or the firm and a distinctive figure). Syndicated copies grouped by near-duplicate text.
measures.label: Share of coverage

measures.definition: Of the later documents on a sub-question it shares, the share that cite it.
measures.how: Citations from reference lists (GROBID 0.9.1) matched to the map’s titles, and from the text when a later document names the firm and the title.
measures.label: Cited by later work

measures.cite: SPICED: Wright, Pei, Jurgens and Augenstein, EMNLP 2022.
measures.definition: Its share of the map’s new findings: results no earlier document in the map states.
measures.how: A finding is new unless an earlier document holds a sentence the matcher judges to state the same information: a shared figure and a SPICED score of 3.5 or more, or a score of 4 or more without one.
measures.label: New findings

measures.cite: Barron, Huang, Spang and DeDeo, PNAS 2018.
measures.definition: How much later documents keep to what it said, minus how far it broke from what came before. Above zero, later work kept to it.
measures.how: Resonance over each document’s mix of sub-questions, five documents either side in time order. Later scholars renamed resonance to avoid implying cause.
measures.label: Staying power

measures.cite: Robinson and Goodman, Annals of Internal Medicine 2011.
measures.definition: Of the earlier documents by others on its sub-questions, the share it cites. Counted once for each of its documents, so the basis is in possible citations.
measures.how: The prior research citation index, applied to the map.
measures.label: Earlier work cited

measures.definition: Share of coverage minus share of new findings, in percentage points. Above zero, it was heard more than it added.
measures.how: The difference of the two posterior shares, drawn together.
measures.label: Coverage minus contribution

measures.definition: Of its claims repeated in articles, the share repeated with figures, hedges and causal strength unchanged.
measures.label: Pickups kept intact

measures.definition: Of its claims repeated in articles, the share the Evidence Hedge engine flags. Read it next to the share of its claims flagged, in the line below.
measures.label: Pickups of flagged claims

measures.definition: Of its claims to be first that can be checked, the share an earlier document in the map contradicts on every stated method, population and setting.
measures.label: “First” claims contradicted

measures.definition: Of its findings, the share no earlier document in the map states.
measures.label: Findings that were new

findings.name: Who cites whom
findings.result: 12 citations among 86 documents; 0 cross from one organization to another. Organizations here cite news, government data and research outside the map, and their own earlier editions.

findings.name: Earlier literature the map is missing
findings.result: 54 earlier documents in the map and 485 earlier works cited by its documents, with no work on both lists. Under independence that implies about 26,729 earlier works (interval 7,979 to 92,734), but most cited works are not on this question, so the figure is not used: originality verdicts rest on the depth of the map instead.

findings.name: Expected but uncited, and whether it leans contrary
findings.result: Needs 30 cross-organization citations before and after the window to train and validate a ranker; the map has 2 and 10. The stance test runs on the ranker’s output, so it waits too.

findings.name: Authority without evidence
findings.result: 12 citation paths, all within one organization’s series; 6 end in a document with its own data. With no citation between organizations there is no network to judge.

findings.name: How long a finding goes on being restated
findings.result: 155 findings were restated by later documents. Half stopped being restated within 1.1 years (Kaplan-Meier). Flagged findings: hazard ratio 0.79 (95% interval 0.57 to 1.10), no clear difference from unflagged ones (Cox).

findings.name: Pickup that begets pickup
findings.result: A Hawkes process needs 20 independent articles for one report; news links are not in yet.

findings.name: Is overreach rewarded
findings.result: The plan needs 60 repeated claims in 20 reports; the map has 0. Nothing is estimated.

limits: The map is one cluster of one corpus: the documents organizations in this field put on their own websites, collected in November 2026. What they did not post, or posted behind forms that were not filled, is not here.
The question was found by grouping documents automatically. Its edges are soft, and a document on two questions sits in only one map.
Most claims are judged new because the matcher needs a near-paraphrase to call a claim old. That favors precision over recall: an idea restated in new words counts as new.
Coverage comes from CC-NEWS, which holds little of the trade press these organizations appear in, so every coverage figure is a floor.
A pooled estimate for an organization with one or two documents says more about the field than about the organization.

models.assumes: Organizations’ true rates come from one shared beta distribution. Its mean and strength are learned from all organizations together and averaged over, not fixed at one best guess, so the intervals keep that uncertainty and the fit holds when every count is zero.
models.cite: Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., section 5.3; Efron and Morris 1975.
models.fails: An organization unlike the rest is pulled toward them; with fewer than three organizations no shared distribution is learned and each rate stands alone.
models.name: Small counts
models.what: Every rate is estimated with a hierarchical beta-binomial model: each organization’s rate is pulled toward the field in proportion to how little data it has. Values are posterior medians with 95% intervals.

models.assumes: Every article could be found by every source, and no article leaves or joins during the search. With two lists, that the lists find articles independently.
models.cite: Fienberg 1972; International Working Group for Disease Monitoring and Forecasting 1995; Chapman 1951.
models.fails: Sources that index the same outlets find the same articles and make the missing count look small. With one list nothing can be said, and the share is over what was found.
models.name: Articles no source found
models.what: The discovery sources are treated as overlapping lists of the same articles. How often they find the same article tells how many articles none of them found, as disease surveillance counts unreported cases.

models.assumes: As above, and that a cited document is on the question.
models.fails: When the map’s documents cite almost nothing the overlap is near zero and the estimate has no upper bound.
models.name: Earlier literature the map is missing
models.what: The same method on two lists of earlier documents: the documents collected for the map, and those cited by the map’s documents.

models.assumes: Sub-question mixes describe what a document is about, and time order is known.
models.cite: Barron, Huang, Spang and DeDeo, PNAS 2018.
models.fails: The newest documents have no five successors and get no value; undated documents are left out; a poor sub-question grouping moves every value.
models.name: Staying power
models.what: Novelty is how far a document’s mix of sub-questions departs from the five documents before it; transience, how far from the five after it. Resonance, shown as staying power, is novelty minus transience. Organizations’ means are pooled toward the field.

models.assumes: A sub-question’s words stand for its demand in news, and the crawl holds a steady mix of outlets.
models.cite: Cameron and Trivedi, Regression Analysis of Count Data, 2nd ed.
models.fails: Common words count unrelated news; CC-NEWS under-holds trade press; three to nine years per sub-question is a short series.
models.name: Open ground
models.what: News demand for each sub-question (its label’s words counted in CC-NEWS, scaled by the size of each month’s crawl) is modeled with a negative binomial regression on the documents published that year. A sub-question’s demand gap is its mean standardized residual over the window: above zero, more demand than the documents predict.

models.assumes: Demand is steady between change points.
models.fails: Nine yearly points rarely support more than one change.
models.name: When a question saturated
models.what: Change points in each sub-question’s yearly demand, by binary segmentation with a Poisson likelihood and a Bayesian information criterion penalty.

models.assumes: Everything a report shares is held fixed; claim-level confounders are measured.
models.cite: VanderWeele and Ding 2017; Chernozhukov et al. 2018; Wager and Athey 2018.
models.fails: Below 60 repeated claims in 20 reports nothing is reported. The pilot is far below that.
models.name: Is overreach rewarded
models.what: A conditional logit with report fixed effects asks whether, within one report, overreaching claims are repeated more. Checked with double machine learning, a causal forest by outlet type and E-values. The plan was written before any outcome.

objection.answer: Both are fair. New findings measure contribution to the record, not truth: the engine’s flags sit beside them in the Claims view, and only result-stating claims count. The matcher is strict, so restated ideas count as new; Kyle’s labels will measure how often. Coverage is labeled a floor everywhere it appears, and no organization is named until every input passes its check.
objection.text: “Your ‘new findings’ count sentences no earlier report happens to paraphrase. A firm that writes long reports on a topic nobody else covers wins, whether or not anything in them is true or useful, and your coverage numbers come from a news crawl that misses the trade press our clients read.”
